citations.context: PASS if the memo cites Illinois Rule 1.7(a)(2) (personal interest conflict) and/or Illinois Rule 1.8(i) (related persons) in connection with Lisa Chow's spousal conflict.

first_check.explanation: The 1.7(a)(2) half is correct. It reaches a 'significant risk' of material limitation from 'a personal interest of the lawyer', and Comment [11] specifically covers lawyers related as spouses who represent different clients in the same or related matters. The 1.8(i) half is mischaracterized. Illinois RPC 1.8(i) bars acquiring a proprietary interest in the cause of action and has nothing to do with 'related persons'. The only 'related persons' definition in Illinois 1.8 is in paragraph (c), on gifts. No paragraph of Illinois Rule 1.8 deals with spousal or family-relationship conflicts between lawyers. Because the rubric uses 'and/or', citing 1.7(a)(2) alone suffices, but the 1.8(i) description is wrong.
first_check.evidence_excerpt: Rule 1.8(i): "A lawyer shall not acquire a proprietary interest in the cause of action or subject matter of litigation the lawyer is conducting for a client..."; Rule 1.7 cmt. [11]: "a lawyer related to another lawyer, e.g., as parent, child, sibling or spouse, ordinarily may not represent a client in a matter where that lawyer is representing another party, unless each client gives informed consent."

second_check.explanation: The finding holds. I read the official Illinois Supreme Court text of Ill. RPC 1.8 (extracted from the PDF). Paragraph (i) reads: "(i) A lawyer shall not acquire a proprietary interest in the cause of action or subject matter of litigation the lawyer is conducting for a client, except that the lawyer may: (1) acquire a lien authorized by law ... and (2) contract with a client for a reasonable contingent fee in a civil case." It says nothing about related persons or spouses. The only 'related persons' language in Rule 1.8 is in paragraph (c), the gift rule: "For purposes of this paragraph, related persons include a spouse, child, grandchild, parent..." That definition applies only to substantial gifts and instruments, not to conflicts between lawyers who are married to each other. Nothing in Illinois Rule 1.8 or its comments governs spousal conflicts between lawyers. The '1.8(i) related persons' label appears to be carried over from an older ABA numbering and does not match current Illinois text. The 1.7(a)(2) half was not disputed, and the rubric's 'and/or' means 1.7(a)(2) alone would satisfy it. Still, the 1.8(i) description is wrong, so MISCHARACTERIZED stands for that half.

citations.cited_for: Screening of lawyers with prior-firm conflicts to cure imputation
citations.context: PASS if the memo discusses that Illinois Rule 1.10(a)(2) (or equivalent) permits screening of lawyers whose conflict arises from prior-firm representation

first_check.correct_citation: Ill. R. Prof'l Conduct 1.10(e) (equivalent to ABA Model Rule 1.10(a)(2))
first_check.explanation: Illinois RPC 1.10(a) is a single paragraph with no subparagraph (a)(2). In Illinois, lateral-hire screening for a lawyer disqualified under Rule 1.9 is in Rule 1.10(e): imputation is avoided if that lawyer is timely screened and gets no part of the fee. The '1.10(a)(2)' numbering matches the ABA Model Rule, whose screening exception covers conflicts arising from a prior firm. I know the ABA text only from search-result summaries, because americanbar.org returned 403. The substance is correct, since Illinois does permit screening to cure a lateral's prior-firm conflict, and the rubric hedges with '(or equivalent)'. But the Illinois subdivision cited does not exist.
first_check.evidence_excerpt: Ill. RPC 1.10(e): "When a lawyer becomes associated with a firm, no lawyer associated in the firm shall knowingly represent a person in a matter in which that lawyer is disqualified under Rule 1.9 unless the personally disqualified lawyer is timely screened from any participation in the matter and is apportioned no part of the fee therefrom."

second_check.explanation: The finding holds. I read the official Illinois text of RPC 1.10 ("Adopted July 1, 2009, effective January 1, 2010"). Paragraph (a) is a single undivided paragraph with no (a)(1) or (a)(2): "(a) While lawyers are associated in a firm, none of them shall knowingly represent a client when any one of them practicing alone would be prohibited from doing so by Rules 1.7 or 1.9, unless the prohibition is based on a personal interest of the prohibited lawyer..." Lateral-hire screening is in paragraph (e): "(e) When a lawyer becomes associated with a firm, no lawyer associated in the firm shall knowingly represent a person in a matter in which that lawyer is disqualified under Rule 1.9 unless the personally disqualified lawyer is timely screened from any participation in the matter and is apportioned no part of the fee therefrom." So the proposition is substantively correct: Illinois does allow screening to cure a lateral's prior-firm conflict. But 'Illinois Rule 1.10(a)(2)' cites a subdivision that does not exist. The correct cite is Ill. RPC 1.10(e); the (a)(2) numbering is the ABA Model Rule's. The rubric's '(or equivalent)' hedge softens this, and the error could arguably be called a minor pinpoint defect. Because the cited Illinois subdivision is nonexistent rather than a wrong page, I keep WRONG_CITATION_REAL_CASE.
